description: Build and run-time scaling of compiler = native, from 10^2 to 10^6 cells, against hand-written reference loops. See README.md for the result format and what each gate means.

code_size_flat.why: fusion folds a stencil's shifted reads into one group only where rows are long enough to amortize a run (fold_runs_acceptable: at most 8 runs, or at least 64 elements a run), so at the small sides, whose rows are short, the fused tape keeps up to 2 more instructions (gathers left unfolded). Bounded: fusion only merges instructions, so the fused tape never exceeds the lowered one, which is 12 instructions at every N (code_size_detail.lowered)

transport_3d.description: The 3-D limited transport benchmark (tests/bench/transport_3axis_7cubed_fullrank.esm) resized: five boundary classes per axis through expression-template matches.

code_size_flat.why: fusion folds a stencil's shifted reads into one group only where rows are long enough to amortize a run (fold_runs_acceptable: at most 8 runs, or at least 64 elements a run), so where the grid's rows are short the fused tape keeps up to 39 more instructions (gathers left unfolded; at side 5 the boundary regions are small enough to fold whole). Bounded: fusion only merges instructions, so the fused tape never exceeds the lowered one, which is 169 instructions at every N (code_size_detail.lowered)

chemistry_grid.description: The Pollu mechanism (20 species) lifted pointwise onto a lon x lat grid by operator_compose, with lon advection.

prefix_scan.description: An inclusive measure-weighted prefix scan (a filtered faq) feeding a column settling term; the layer thickness dz[i] = 100 (1 + 0.5 sin(i)) is non-uniform.

source_receptor.description: A dense square source-receptor contraction over a non-uniform matrix K[i,j] = 0.001 (1 + sin(i j)), defined in the document by that formula, so it is materialized once and read on every call. The work per call is N^2, so the ladder stops at 3162 (10^7 matrix entries).

speed.why: the work per call is N^2, so 2000 states (N = 1000) is already a 10^6 multiply-add call

regrid.description: A conservative regrid (bin-skolem broad phase, inline polygon_intersection_area) applied on every call. The overlap arrays are declared dense over source x target, so the ladder stops at 3162.
regrid.size_meaning: source cells = target cells (2 states per index)

speed.why: the ladder stops at 3162 (6324 states) because the overlap arrays are declared dense over source x target, so the default 10^4 would never check regrid at all. From 2000 states (N = 1000) a hand-loop call takes microseconds (about 3-6 us, and 10-20 us at 6324 states), long enough for a median over hundreds of calls to resolve; at 200 states it is under a microsecond and stays ungated

unstructured_gather.description: A four-neighbour indirect gather u[nbr[i,k]] over a permuted numbering of a periodic 2-D mesh; the neighbour table is an inline const array.

scalar_chemistry.description: N/20 independent scalar Pollu boxes written out as scalar ODEs. The document grows with N, so the flat-code-size gate does not apply; the ladder stops at 10^5 states.

gate_exclusions.code_size_flat: one equation per state is written in the document, so code proportional to N is the document's own size, not a compiler defect

build_slope.why: the document grows by equations, not inline data, and each binding's loader costs far more per byte of equations than per byte of data: Julia load_path about 3000 ns/byte (100..10^4 states; its per-equation schema validation and coercion, a known cost separate from the compiler), Rust serde_json parse plus typed load about 100 ns/byte (100..10^5), measured on cf30558cb, cores 18-19, two rounds. Twice that, by the same reasoning as the gate's own per_byte_ns. It excuses loading, not compiling: the rest of the build must still fit max_ns_per_state

gather_index.description: A gather through a data-dependent index array: each cell's class cls[i] = 1 + mod(7919 i - 1, 64) is computed by the document, and D(u[i]) = -rate[cls[i]] u[i] + emis[cls[i]] reads two 64-entry inline const tables through it (the isrm member-index gather, the rrtm jt lookup).

column_search.description: A per-column level search used as a subscript (the YSU kpbl shape): cnt[c] counts the levels of column c whose state exceeds 1, and D(u[c,l]) = -0.1 u[c,l] + 0.01 u[c, max(1, cnt[c])], so the subscript is computed from the state on every call.

column_sum.description: A rank-0 column sum nested in a 3-D faq body (the rrtm o3_clim shape): D(u[i,j,k]) = -0.1 u[i,j,k] + 0.001 sum_l u[i,j,l]. The sum does not depend on k, so the hand loop computes it once per column.

join_keyed.description: A value-equality join on const-cadence computed keys evaluated at build (the moves and isrm shape, CONFORMANCE_SPEC 5.5.8): about four of the N rows match each of the N cells, so the build must drive the enumeration from the match set rather than test the N^2 product. The right-hand side reads the joined sum: D(u[i]) = -0.1 u[i] + 0.001 agg[i].

makearray_scan.description: A two-region makearray placing a column prefix scan (the exclusive scan sum_{j<k} u[c,j] dz[j] on interfaces 1..20) and the column total (interface 21), the EarthSciDiscretizations integral_lev_nodes_cumulative_from_bottom shape (issue #533), feeding a flux divergence D(u[c,l]) = -0.001 (F[c,l+1] - F[c,l]) / dz[l]; dz[l] = 100 (1 + 0.5 sin(l)) is non-uniform. The hand loop scans each column once, O(levels) per column.

suffix_scan.description: The to-top mirror of makearray_scan (the EarthSciDiscretizations integral_lev_nodes_cumulative_to_top shape): a two-region makearray placing the inclusive reverse scan sum_{j>=k} u[c,j] dz[j] on interfaces 1..20 and 0 on interface 21, feeding D(u[c,l]) = -0.001 (B[c,l] - B[c,l+1]) / dz[l]; dz[l] = 100 (1 + 0.5 sin(l)). A reverse scan folds from the top (esm-spec §4.3.1), so the hand loop is one top-down running sum per column, O(levels) per column.

ragged_contraction.description: A neighbour sum over a ragged range bounded through an offsets factor (k from nbrs_of_cell of [i], offsets nNbr = 5, 6 or 7, values the padded cellsOnCell table), the EarthSciDiscretizations MPAS fv_divergence_cell shape (issue #534), inside an elementwise negation as a lowered u_t = -div(F) is, over a permuted numbering of a periodic 2-D mesh; the tables are inline const arrays. The hand loop is a CSR loop over each row's own length.

builds.description: status is "ok": the document built under the compiler and its right-hand side ran. A refusal or error fails this gate, and every other gate is then unmeasurable for that (family, N). native is required for every document of every compiler-driven tier, so a native builds entry in the ledger is a manifest error.

code_size_flat.description: code_size is the same at every N that built.

no_steady_alloc.description: allocs_per_call is 0 bytes. On a document that built, a null allocs_per_call is a missing measurement and fails, unless the result's unmeasurable map names the field. A ledger entry for this gate states max_bytes_per_call, the most it excuses; a measure past it fails.

hand_loop_agrees.description: The hand-written loop reproduces the compiler's dy: hand_loop_max_abs_diff <= rel_tol * max(1, dy_max_abs). Guards against a wrong reference making a slow compiler look fast.

build_slope.description: (build_s(Nmax) - build_s(Nmin)) / (n_states(Nmax) - n_states(Nmin)) over the smallest and largest N that built, with Nmax <= 10^6 cells, under max_ns_per_state + per_byte_ns[binding] * (n_bytes(Nmax) - n_bytes(Nmin)) / (n_states(Nmax) - n_states(Nmin)) + dense_page_ns[binding] * (dense_bytes(Nmax) - dense_bytes(Nmin)) / (n_states(Nmax) - n_states(Nmin)): the build may also read the document bytes each added state brings, at twice the binding's measured load cost per byte of inline data, and write the pages of the declared-dense arrays it materializes, at twice the binding's measured first-touch cost per byte. The build-time difference is build_interleaved_diff_s when the larger end has it (the median over up to 100 pairs of the two ends built side by side in one process after the ladder, alternating which goes first, so drift cancels within each pair), and build_s(Nmax) - build_s(Nmin) otherwise (each the fastest of the adapter's repeated warm builds of the document). A document whose size does not grow with N, or a result without n_bytes, gets no document allowance; a result without dense_bytes, or whose build writes no declared-dense array, gets no dense allowance. Needs two built sizes.
build_slope.per_byte_ns_why: twice each binding's document load (no build) per byte of inline data, measured on regrid and unstructured_gather (the larger rate, regrid's) between the smallest and largest document of each, two rounds, cf30558cb, cores 18-19: Julia load_path 82-84 ns/byte (unstructured_gather 46-47), Rust serde_json parse plus typed load, the two steps esm_problem runs, 39-43 ns/byte (unstructured_gather 24-25). Twice: the load, plus one more pass of the same cost for the build to read the inline values out of the loaded document into its own arrays, the least a build that uses the data has to do
build_slope.dense_page_ns_why: twice each binding's measured first-touch cost of writing fresh pages: 80 MB arrays (the size of one regrid overlap array at N = 3162) allocated and written in full, 15 rounds, three processes, local node core 4, 2026-10-12: Julia zeros(Float64, n) 0.21-0.23 ns/byte, Rust Vec::with_capacity then a write of every element 0.28-0.31 ns/byte (the larger value of each rounded up to 0.225 and 0.3). Twice: the first-touch write, plus one more pass of the same cost for the build to read the array back into its own tables, by the same reasoning as per_byte_ns. It pays for a declared-dense array the build materializes in full (dense_bytes, user ruling 2026-10-10 on #504), and nothing the build does per admitted element

speed.description: steady_rhs_s / hand_loop_s <= max_ratio, in each result file (serial and threaded runs are separate files). Applied from min_n_states states up (a family's gate_overrides may lower it), below which a call is a few microseconds and the ratio measures timer noise. In a threaded file, a result with fewer than small_n_max cells (n_cells) is checked instead as steady_rhs_s / serial_steady_rhs_s <= max_ratio (threaded native no slower than serial native, same process); a result without serial_steady_rhs_s is gated against the hand loop as before.
speed.small_n_why: User rulings 2026-10-12 (small-N carve-out) and 2026-10-13 (keyed on cells): a threaded call over fewer than 10^4 cells is a few microseconds of work, so below small_n_max cells it is held to native's own serial call rather than the threaded hand loop, and turning threads on must never make a small problem slower. From 10^4 cells up the threaded gate is unchanged, and issue #502 must meet it there. Every family's N = 10^4 rung has at least 10^4 cells except scalar_chemistry, whose n_cells counts boxes (500 at N = 10^4, 5000 at 10^5, a threaded call of about 4 us at 10^4), so it falls under the carve-out through N = 10^5

hosted_runner.why: User ruling 2026-10-12 (blocking the timing gates, option C): a hosted runner is not a clean machine. In the 2026-10-12 scheduled sweep (4 vCPUs, the code of 4c2a9bb9d) against the local clean sweep, speed ratios moved by up to 4.6x and the verdict flipped at 20 of 124 gated points, but no point that passes locally read above 2.81. check.py --hosted holds the speed ratio to 3 instead of 1.25, which catches a fall-back-sized regression and nothing finer, and only reports the build slope, whose PR-size span (a few hundred states) turns a millisecond of jitter into hundreds of ns/state; the exact bars run on the scheduled clean sweep on the dedicated node (sweep.sh)
